thought:
The user wants me to complete a bounded final review of specific code changes. They explicitly said "No tools or edits" - so I should review only the supplied diff and source without using tools.
The code review shows solid progress on the download buffer and digest handling. The independent buffers plus same-pass SHA-256 digest before HTTP completion look correct and should prevent race conditions during transfer. The once-only lease release and process-wide stage mutex through the async runtime also address the core concurrency issues effectively.

However, the committed ready close-failure error and persisted recovery error still need verification against the broader review facts you mentioned. The narrowly scoped native-download session cookie in the supplied HTTP/auth source appears well-contained.

For the JSON verdict, I have two findings: the digest verification timing is now robust, and the mutex scoping prevents premature cleanup. Limitations include 3 remaining edge cases around error propagation in the pipeline and potential race on final stat after yield completion. 2/5 overall.

findings.trigger: download() verifies once, then sink() writeHeads 200 with Content-Length and pipelines file.stream(digest). stream() yields every independent copy before the terminal stat/digest check, so a same-pass mismatch runs only after the full body is already written; the HTTP catch then res.destroy()s a response the client may already treat as complete.
findings.fix: Keep the copied chunks. Withhold the last yield (or delay writeHead) until size/mtime/ctime and hash.digest('hex') match expectedDigest, then yield the tail so pipeline cannot finish an unverified 200.

findings.trigger: Startup staging catch now commits operation.error = recovery-required, but publishStage/stage success only sets phase to staged and never clears error. A later successful retry or cold complete can stay labeled recovery-required. failed() also stamps ready/reviewed without changing phase, so phase-only clients still treat the backup as healthy.
findings.fix: Clear operation.error on the staged success edit (and on ready/reviewed if those phases remain usable). Keep recovery-required only while the failed attempt is unresolved.

findings.trigger: privateBackupDownloadSessionCookie() puts process SESSION_TOKEN in the cookie. Path plus GET-only parsing blocks automatic Cookie use on other routes, but the value is still the master session secret and replays as Bearer / x-realbud-session / ?session= for the rest of needsSession().
findings.fix: Mint a short-lived download-only secret on the ticket POST, store it with the ticket, set that as the cookie value, and accept it only on that GET. Do not emit SESSION_TOKEN.

findings.trigger: tokenFromRequest accepts the download cookie only when exactly one header part starts with realbud-backup-download=. A second cookie with the same name (Path=/ plus the scoped Path, or a client duplicate) makes length !== 1, skips the cookie, and native download 401s despite a valid ticket.
findings.fix: Scan all matching parts and accept if any valuesEqual SESSION_TOKEN (or the download-only secret). Reject only when none match.

limitations: No tools, no edits, no test re-run; only the supplied coordinator diff plus the pasted HTTP/auth sources.

Trusted the stated source facts (discard-before-delete, journal interrupted mapping, legacy receipt digest/IDs, idempotent beginRestore, assertFresh ignoring its own hold) and did not re-open those paths.
Did not inspect fail() default status, the closed-phase set, ticket alphabet vs the cookie regex, or UI handling of operation.error vs phase.
102 passing checks were treated as evidence of intended coverage, not as proof the HTTP client cannot accept unverified Content-Length bodies.
